why: 0.4 AND 0.5 CANNOT BE TOLD APART ON THIS ARM, for every input the type
admits.  `durationMs` is an `unsigned int`, so `durationMs * 8.0` is an
exact integer in a double for every value up to 2^53, and adding any
constant strictly between 0 and 1 to an integer leaves the truncation
unchanged.  The rounding term is therefore unobservable HERE and is
observable on the analog arm, where the multiplier is 9.6 and the
product has a fraction -- and that mutation, `9.6` truncated instead of
rounded, IS caught.
Kept as the pair to it: the two entries together say that the +0.5 is
load-bearing on one arm and not on the other, which is a property of the
two rates and not of the test.  `+ 1.5` is mutated separately and is
caught, so the term is not untested -- only this VALUE of it is
indistinguishable.

why: SIXTEEN OF THE TWENTY-ONE STORES AGREE WITH THE CONSTRUCTOR, and these
three are among them.  `VPcmFloModem::VPcmFloModem` has already written
`terminateJa`, `terminateCp` and `terminateCpNot` to zero
(src/pump/v90/VPcmFloModemCtor.cpp), the object under construction is
reached by nothing else between the two, and no side effect can restore
the storage's old bytes -- so removing the second write leaves exactly
the value the first one put there.  No observation of memory can
separate the two spellings.
The duplication is the ORIGINAL'S and the object has both, so the
source keeps both: the second tier can see the difference even though
the first cannot.  This entry is conditional on VPcmFloModemCtor.cpp
keeping its own store, and if that ever changes this mutation will
start being caught, which is the notification.
The five stores that CONTRADICT the constructor -- nofBitsPerSymbol,
minNofTransmitSequences and three of the six flags -- are the ones that
carry information, and every one of those is mutated above and caught.
